top_choice_rationale: P001 (B001, Helpman and Melitz) credits one identifiable mechanism: productivity differences across firms drive selection into exporting and foreign investment, and trade reallocates activity across firms. The core papers (Melitz 2003; Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple 2004) are over twenty years old. Their sharp, falsifiable predictions have been tested repeatedly in firm-level data from many countries. Where the baseline failed in detail, the literature extended the model and kept the selection logic. That is the kind of mature, credible evidence base I value as a metascience researcher. The two-name attribution is defensible if the citation is kept narrow, naming selection and reallocation and not claiming settled welfare magnitudes or the whole firm-level trade programme. The main risk is the omission of Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum. That is a judgment about what counts as the discovery, and the scientific background can acknowledge those precursors. Agreement among the eleven simulated round-2 files is not evidence of merit, so I rest this ranking on content and not on the count. P000 is ranked last because the slate's only award proposal rests on a mature, well-tested and attributable discovery, so no-award is the weaker option.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no tie to Helpman or Melitz. Disclosed for transparency: my metascience background may lead me to weight robustness and replication evidence heavily, and I share an SSE affiliation with some colleagues who are not candidates.
